mechanism: Phenobarbital induces CYP2C9 and CYP3A4, increasing isoniazid metabolism and reducing its serum concentrations, while isoniazid inhibits phenobarbital metabolism via CYP2C9, potentially increasing phenobarbital levels and toxicity.
action: Monitor isoniazid and phenobarbital serum concentrations closely; consider alternative antituberculosis agents or increased isoniazid dosing; assess for phenobarbital toxicity signs (ataxia, sedation, nystagmus).
